A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KaSA research. All 39 pages of each version, including Appendices A–H, support comparison. Relocated sections, tables, and figures can be matched without material evidence gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original KaSA evaluations on GLUE, E2E, instruction-following tasks, MT-Bench, and commonsense reasoning, together with ablations and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the DeBERTa and E2E evaluations relocated to Appendix F.

M1.justification: SVD truncation, the trainable singular-value adaptation, and the three-part training objective remain unchanged. Appendix A corrects the implementation description of an existing parameter; it does not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same GLUE tasks, E2E dataset, four synthetic instruction-following datasets, Alpaca/MT-Bench, and eight commonsense reasoning tasks. The DeBERTa and NLG material moves to Appendix F without changing coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments. The relocated DeBERTa and GPT-2 tables retain their baselines; instruction-following comparisons retain FFT, LoRA, PiSSA, and MiLoRA, and the rank-128 comparison still includes DoRA and CorDA.

E3.justification: The reported datasets, metrics, model sizes, training budgets, ranks, judging procedures, and Appendix E hyperparameters are unchanged. Moving the NLG protocol into Appendix F.2 does not alter its settings.

E4.justification: Component ablations, rank sweeps, initialization comparisons, regularization curves, sensitivity tests, efficiency analyses, and case studies are retained. v1 Appendices F.1–F.7 become v2 F.3–F.9 without substantive changes.

E5.justification: v2 Table 2 removes all 80 reported ± uncertainty values and 60 individual p-values from v1 Table 4, covering four models and five instruction-following evaluations. The text still claims p < 0.05 in 9 of 12 MT-Bench comparisons. This substantially reduces statistical reporting; GLUE and E2E run-count disclosures remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Performance point estimates, rankings, plots, and qualitative examples are unchanged, but concrete statistical result entries are removed. For example, LLaMA3 LoRA's MT-Bench result changes from 4.19±0.3 with p=0.020 in v1 Table 4 to only 4.19 in v2 Table 2.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, and Appendix G derivations are retained. Equations 19 and 23 rewrite initialization arrows from W → ΔW to ΔW ← W, preserving their meaning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: knowledge-aware SVD adaptation, efficient task-specific modules, superiority claims over FFT and 14 PEFT baselines, and release of synthetic datasets. Wording edits do not change their scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning noisy singular components, task-relevant knowledge, initialization, and regularization remain unchanged. Appendix F retains the truncation tradeoff and proposed future work on adaptive rank selection and orthogonality.

D1.justification: Appendix A, Algorithm 1, now stores delta_sigma directly as nn.Parameter and applies torch.diag during the forward pass; v1 applied torch.diag when assigning the parameter. This corrects parameter registration in the pseudocode. Hyperparameters, hardware disclosures, prompts, and code/data access information are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference list and substantive related-work discussion are unchanged, including positioning against LoRA, PiSSA, MiLoRA, and other SVD-based approaches.

P1.justification: v2 moves the DeBERTa discussion and NLG section into Appendices F.1–F.2, updates cross-references, adds acknowledgments, expands author-role footnotes, and changes the publication header. Most prose is retained with limited wording edits.

P2.justification: The DeBERTa and GPT-2 tables move from main-text Tables 2–3 to appendix Tables 11–12. The instruction-following table is reformatted with larger text and fewer annotations. Other changes concern placement and pagination; all 18 figures are retained without substantive visual changes.

improvement.justification: The pseudocode correction and more readable instruction-following table provide limited benefits. However, removing its uncertainty values and individual p-values makes the retained significance claim less verifiable. With the method, point estimates, and other evidence essentially unchanged, this produces a limited net decline in empirical transparency.
